messages:
alice.martin: Pushed a quick profiling dump for the cross-device kernel picker. Focus: L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100, sequence-length dependent paths + KV cache behavior. TL;DR: some unexpected perf cliffs around seq=384 on L4/T4.

ben_ng: Nice — link?

alice.martin: https://internal.redwood/tmp/prof/1793045678/trace.html (quick summary pasted below)

carla: paste the key numbers here plz, can't access the page from this meeting room.

alice.martin: Summary:
- Model: 7B transformer, causal, 2048 context allowed
- Workloads: (A) short chats seq=64, (B) med seq=256, (C) long seq=512 streaming
- Devices: L4 (40GB), T4 (16GB), A10 (24GB), A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB)
- Kernel presets: small-attn, flash+fused-kv, gemm-int8, block-sparse (experiment)

Key perf snapshots (tokens/s for gen loop, single-stream):
- seq=64: H100=210k, A100=180k, A10=75k, L4=60k, T4=35k
- seq=256: H100=95k, A100=82k, A10=38k, L4=28k, T4=18k
- seq=512: H100=42k, A100=36k, A10=14k, L4=11k, T4=6k

Notable: L4/T4 drop sharply between seq=320-400. p99 latency jumps and memory churn visible in KV cache ops.

daniel_h: Is that with fused KV on or off? We had heuristics that pick fused-kv for small-GPUs.

alice.martin: These runs used the current autotuner: fused-kv enabled for non-H100/A100 by default; matmul kernel = gemm_int8 on L4/A10/T4 when quantized. But for seq>384 the runtime falls back to chunked KV copy path which allocates temp buffers repeatedly — that's the churn.

esther_y: Can you paste the autotuner rule snippet?

alice.martin: Sure:
```
autotune.rules:
  - name: prefer_flash_for_large_hw
    if: device in [H100, A100] and seq_len >= 128
    pick: flash_fwd + no_fused_kv
  - name: small_gpu_fused_kv
    if: device in [L4, A10, T4] and model_quant == int8
    pick: gemm_int8 + fused_kv
  - name: seq_split_fallback
    if: seq_len > 384 and device in [L4, T4]
    pick: chunked_kv_copy + small_attn
```

ben_ng: That seq_split_fallback is likely too blunt. chunked_kv_copy allocates O(seq) temporaries per token; on small heaps that's camping the allocator and triggering reclamation/paging.

carla: Could we instead stream KV shards to pinned CPU memory and memcpy async? I think we tried that in 2023 for T4 and it helped.

daniel_h: Streaming to CPU + pinned memcpy helped bandwidth but added latency variance. For medium seqs (256-384) it was net-positive on T4/L4 before, but we removed it because it regressed A10 in some cases.

alice.martin: Right. The profiling trace shows high CUDA malloc/free rates around fallback transition. Also kernel selection logs: we incorrectly switch off the flash-attn path for A10 at seq=320 due to a conservative memory estimate in the selector.

esther_y: Could the selector use a more accurate sequence-length dependent memory model? Like estimate KV cached size = hidden_dim * seq_len * 2 + safety_margin and prefer in-place KV when < device_free*0.7?

alice.martin: Yep — prototype rule attached in trace folder: it computes kv_bytes and checks with allocator peak stats. Early numbers look promising: prevents fallback for A10 up to seq=448, throughput +20% for seq in [256,448].

perf-bot: perf-regression-check: noted previous A10 baseline at seq=384 = 30k tok/s, current = 28k tok/s (−6.7%). Will post CI diffs for the kernel-picker change if we modify rules.

ben_ng: For safety we should add canary: when switching off chunked_kv_copy, keep a rolling histogram of p99 and OOMs for N=2k requests before full rollout. Also add per-device safety thresholds.

carla: Agree. Also add a soft cap on temporary bytes per-stream: if temp_allocs > X within Y tokens, force fallback. That would avoid the long-tail allocator thrash.

daniel_h: I can add a patch to the picker: more precise mem model + soft cap + pinned-cpu async memcpy option gated behind feature flag. I'll open a PR and tag @alice.martin for perf numbers to attach.

alice.martin: Thanks. I'll also add targeted traces for L4/A10 seq=320/384/448 with and without fused-kv to reproduce local.

esther_y: Heads up — if we change autoscale batcher heuristics, the batching window interacts with KV cache locality. Keep an eye on batch_size distributions in the new traces.

alice.martin: Good call. Will collect batch histograms as well.

ben_ng: Cool. Next action items: @daniel_h PR for selector + safety caps, @alice.martin extra traces uploaded, we run canary for A10/L4/T4 for 48h with perf-bot monitoring. :thumbsup:

carla: ping me if the canary shows p99 regressions, I'll roll back rules in the runtime flagger.

alice.martin: Will do. Thanks all!
